title: Keep work and resume on stage timeout; split multi-part plans
summary: When a producer or verifier stage hits its deadline, keep the worktree edits and write a progress note. Record the job as timed out rather than failed, and let a retry resume from the kept work. Planning should yield one item per separate part of a request. The audience is the Athena operator, who loses 20–30 minutes of work per timeout.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added and cargo test/clippy/fmt criteria.
Criteria check kept edits, resumed retry and recorded outcome by running tests.
Docs and changelog written for an outside reader.
One change; both parts are tied to the same request.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Reading 1 stands; no user replies altered it.
A new timed-out outcome/status is added to records in a backward-compatible way; old killed/failed records still deserialize.
Plan splitting is done in the planning prompt/logic in athena-core plan.rs, not a new planner.
Retry reuses the kept worktree and passes the progress note into the new producer's brief.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test with the fake agent hits a producer deadline after editing files. Afterwards the edits remain in the job worktree, a progress note exists, and the job is recorded as timed out, not failed. Run: cargo test.
A test retries a timed-out job. The new producer starts from the kept work, is given the progress note, and does not start from a clean checkout. Run: cargo test.
A test of a verifier-stage deadline shows it is recorded as timed out, and the retry does not redo the already-passed producer stage. Run: cargo test.
A planning test shows a multi-part request yields one plan item per part, and a single-part request still yields one item. Run: cargo test.
Status and report output distinguishes timed out from failed, and the deadline reason (for example 'deadline of 1800s reached') is kept in the record. Run: cargo test.
Existing records with killed or failed outcomes still deserialize (test covers it). The new outcome is documented and CHANGELOG.md mentions the change.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass with no new warnings.

out_of_scope: Automatic retry scheduling beyond resuming on an explicit retry
departures: Touches the run lifecycle, records schema, retry and planning together, so cost and time are above the reference and verification is somewhat less likely to pass.
urgent_reason: Timeouts discard 20–30 minutes of producer work each time and force redo-work retries; keeping the work cuts that waste.
